Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
The Indian government operates a pension scheme. Which statement about this scheme would be classed as normative?

options.A: To be eligible, individuals must be above the age of 60 and live below the poverty line.
options.B: In January 2020, eligible individuals aged over 70 received 500 rupees per month.
options.C: In 2018, the Supreme Court said the government must review pension payments because they are unrealistic.
options.D: In January 2020, the Indian government announced that it might increase the payment to 1000 rupees per month.

questions.questionText: Economics students have to fill in the gaps in the following passage. ‘The three basic questions arising from the economic problem of scarcity are ......1...... to produce, ......2...... to produce, and ......3...... to produce.’ Which combination is correct?
What is not a function of money?

options.A: It is a medium of exchange.
options.B: It is a store of value.
options.C: It is a unit of account.
options.D: It is a measure of satisfaction.

questions.questionText: The producer of a good with a price-elastic demand observes that a rise in its price is accompanied by a rise in total revenue. What might explain this?

options.A: The good is an inferior good.
options.B: The rise in price was due to an increase in demand for the good.
options.C: The supply of the good was inadequate to meet the demand.
options.D: The supply of the good was price-inelastic.

questions.questionText: What will increase the producer surplus of farmers that grow carrots?

options.A: a decrease in the demand for carrots
options.B: a decrease in the price of carrot seed
options.C: a decrease in the price of cabbage
options.D: a decrease in the subsidy on carrots

questions.questionText: A popular band is due to perform at a music concert in a venue that has a 5000-seat capacity. Recent appearances and the release of a new album have made the band even more popular. D and S represent the original demand and supply curves for concert tickets and D the new demand curve. Which diagram best represents the likely outcome on the market for concert tickets?

options.A: B S D D

questions.questionText: Why does an individual’s demand curve generally slope downwards to the right?

options.A: The additional satisfaction an individual gets from consuming most goods decreases as consumption increases.
options.B: The additional satisfaction an individual gets from consumption decreases as income rises.
options.C: The individual has finite income which is used to attempt to satisfy many wants.
options.D: For most goods the price charged by producers falls as the quantity purchased increases.

questions.questionText: What is price elasticity of supply?

options.A: the change in the quantity supplied when a price changes
options.B: the change in the quantity supplied when demand changes
options.C: the comparison of the proportionate change in supply to the proportionate change in demand
options.D: the comparison of the proportionate change in supply to the proportionate change in price

questions.questionText: What is necessary for consumer surplus to be zero?

options.A: Demand is perfectly elastic.
options.B: Demand is perfectly inelastic.
options.C: Supply is perfectly elastic.
options.D: Supply is perfectly inelastic.

questions.questionText: When will the price mechanism not function as a system for allocating goods?

options.A: when the government bans advertising
options.B: when the government maintains an effective maximum price
options.C: when there is a limited supply of the good
options.D: when there is a powerful company able to set the market price

questions.questionText: The price of a product is above the market equilibrium price. Which combination of changes is certain to result as the market adjusts towards equilibrium? quantity demanded quantity supplied

options.A: falls falls
options.B: falls rises
options.C: rises falls
options.D: rises rises

questions.questionText: What can be concluded about a good with a positive cross-price elasticity of demand?

options.A: Its price will be sensitive to changes in prices of close substitutes.
options.B: Its price will be sensitive to changes in quantity demanded of close substitutes.
options.C: The quantity demanded for this good will be sensitive to changes in prices of close substitutes.
options.D: The quantity demanded for this good will be sensitive to changes in quantity demanded of close substitutes.

questions.questionText: Which row shows the effect of the maximum and minimum prices described in the headings of the table? maximum price maximum price minimum price above below above equilibrium price equilibrium price equilibrium price

options.A: excess demand no effect no effect
options.B: excess supply no effect no effect
options.C: no effect excess demand excess supply
options.D: no effect excess supply excess demand

questions.questionText: A government decides to introduce tolls (charges) to drive on all major roads. What is most likely to happen to the number of journeys made on major roads and on minor roads? journeys on journeys on major roads minor roads

options.A: reduce increase
options.B: reduce no change
options.C: no change increase
options.D: no change no change

questions.questionText: The table shows data from a bus company that was privatised in 2013. passenger journeys revenue year percentage change $000 from previous year (%) 2012 470 +5 2013 495 +2 2014 430 –2 2015 440 –1 What is the most likely conclusion that can be made from the data?

options.A: Average prices were higher in 2012 than 2015.
options.B: Average prices were higher in 2015 than 2014.
options.C: The number of passenger journeys remained the same since privatisation.
options.D: Profits have increased since privatisation.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the market for electricity in a country that has a fixed supply of electricity and introduces a maximum price to make it affordable for poorer households. S price of electricity market price maximum price D O quantity of electricity What will be the effect of this?

options.A: It will encourage producers to build more power stations in the future.
options.B: It will encourage the development of renewable sources of electricity.
options.C: It will increase producer surplus.
options.D: It will increase the probability of power cuts.

questions.questionText: What is an example of a transfer payment?

options.A: government spending on hospitals
options.B: government spending on motorways
options.C: minimum wage
options.D: welfare benefits

questions.questionText: Turkey can produce a good but also imports some of the good from Egypt. The Turkish currency depreciates against the Egyptian currency. How is this most likely to affect production of this good in Egypt and in Turkey? production in Egypt production in Turkey

options.A: decrease decrease
options.B: decrease increase
options.C: increase decrease
options.D: increase increase

questions.questionText: The table shows a country’s total output and its average price in each of three years. output price year (millions) ($)
The diagram shows the change in the supply curve of imports, S–S to curve S–S , after the

The aggregate demand (AD) and aggregate supply (AS) diagram shows an economy in equilibrium at X. In this economy, a severe shortage of raw materials causes a large rise in their price. The effect of this change is shown by a move to which point? AD
Why might a country’s government impose a tax on fuel exports?

options.A: to encourage domestic refineries to increase production
options.B: to improve the country’s trade balance
options.C: to reduce fuel prices for domestic consumers
options.D: to reduce the government’s budget surplus

questions.questionText: What leads to a fall in a country’s terms of trade?

options.A: a fall in the price of exports relative to the price of imports
options.B: a fall in the price of imports relative to the price of exports
options.C: a fall in the quantity of exports relative to the quantity of imports
options.D: a fall in the quantity of imports relative to the quantity of exports

questions.questionText: The diagram has three lines that show the values of an economy’s exports, imports and trade balance between 2011 and 2019. $m + 1 – 2011 2015 2019 year How should the lines be labelled? line 1 line 2 line 3

options.A: exports imports trade balance
options.B: exports trade balance imports
options.C: imports exports trade balance
options.D: imports trade balance exports

questions.questionText: What would be the best policy to increase the value of a currency?

options.A: Impose tariffs on imported goods with price-inelastic demand.
options.B: Increase interest rates.
options.C: Reduce income tax.
options.D: Sell the currency on the foreign exchange markets.

questions.questionText: The central bank of an economy decides to raise interest rates in order to attract capital inflows and improve the financial account of the balance of payments. When is the central bank’s decision least likely to be effective?

options.A: when the currency of the economy is expected to lose its value
options.B: when the economy is politically and economically stable
options.C: when the interest rate of the economy is higher than that of other countries
options.D: when the reserves of foreign currencies held by the central bank are high and rising

questions.questionText: What could be described as an expansionary fiscal policy?

options.A: a decrease in the budget deficit
options.B: a decrease in the budget surplus
options.C: a decrease in the exchange rate
options.D: a decrease in the money supply

questions.questionText: Why will a contractionary monetary policy reduce inflation?

options.A: Banks will lend more.
options.B: Consumers will have higher disposable income.
options.C: Consumers will pay more tax.
options.D: Consumers will save more.

questions.questionText: The government of a country is worried about a large deficit on the current account of its balance of payments and an increasing rate of inflation. The country has a fixed exchange rate for its currency. Which policy measure is most likely to help the government to reduce the current account deficit and lower the rate of inflation?

options.A: devaluation of the currency
options.B: increasing government spending
options.C: decreasing the direct taxes
